subject: Chemistry
title: Polymerization Gone Wrong: The Texas City Disaster
description: A short lesson to help you apply Polymerization Gone Wrong: The Texas City Disaster.

hook.text: In 1947, a ship loaded with ammonium nitrate exploded in Texas City. The blast killed 581 people.

buildup.text: Ammonium nitrate is a fertilizer. Normally safe, it becomes explosive when heated in a confined space.

discovery.text: A small fire on the ship heated the cargo. At 230°C, ammonium nitrate decomposes explosively.

twist.text: The blast was so powerful it created a 4.5-meter tidal wave and knocked two planes out of the sky.

climax.text: The same compound caused the 2020 Beirut explosion. Ammonium nitrate remains one of the most mishandled chemicals.

punchline.text: Fertilizer that becomes a bomb when heated. Same chemical, different fate.

quiz.question: What makes ammonium nitrate dangerous?
options: It decomposes explosively when heated in a confined space
It is always unstable and explodes on contact
It reacts with water to form toxic gas

details.summary: The 1947 Texas City disaster began when ammonium nitrate cargo detonated aboard the SS Grandcamp, triggering a chain of explosions that killed nearly 600 people. Ammonium nitrate can undergo violent decomposition when confined and heated, a risk still demonstrated in modern incidents.
details.whyItMatters: This disaster reshaped industrial safety regulations for ammonium nitrate storage and transport. The chemistry of ammonium nitrate decomposition remains relevant to modern fertilizer safety.
takeaways: Ammonium nitrate is stable but can detonate when confined and heated
The Texas City disaster killed nearly 600 and reshaped safety codes
Ammonium nitrate regulations remain critical for public safety

faq.question: Why is ammonium nitrate used as fertilizer if it can explode?
faq.answer: Under normal conditions, ammonium nitrate is a stable, highly effective nitrogen source for crops. It only becomes dangerous when large quantities are confined, contaminated, or exposed to sustained high temperatures. Proper storage and handling make it safe for agricultural use.

faq.question: Have there been similar ammonium nitrate disasters in recent history?
faq.answer: Yes. The 2020 Beirut port explosion was caused by 2,750 tons of improperly stored ammonium nitrate. The 2013 West, Texas fertilizer plant explosion and the 2001 Toulouse AZF factory disaster were also ammonium nitrate events, highlighting persistent storage safety challenges.
